rationale: Start with a broad organic range to retain early compounds while promoting elution of all 10 compounds within the acquisition window. A moderate gradient time and temperature provide a baseline for identifying crowded regions and guiding subsequent optimization.

Halve the gradient time to reduce the time penalty while testing whether the current resolution margin is sufficient. Keeping composition endpoints and temperature fixed isolates the effect of gradient steepness.

Test an intermediate gradient to recover resolution in the crowded middle cluster without returning to the long retention time of injection 1. This will help locate the best resolution–time tradeoff before adjusting temperature or starting composition.

Increase temperature by 5 °C to test whether temperature-dependent selectivity resolves the remaining close pair while maintaining a zero time penalty. Keep the gradient unchanged to isolate the temperature effect.

The close pair converged as temperature increased, suggesting that a further increase may separate it again after an elution-order reversal. Test 55 °C while retaining the 14-minute gradient to seek full resolution without a time penalty.

Slightly increase gradient steepness relative to injection 5 to test whether the nearly resolved pair separates further after its apparent order reversal. The small slope change should preserve the neighboring resolution margin and keep the time penalty at zero.

Increase gradient steepness slightly again to push the remaining close pair above R = 1.5 while preserving the neighboring pair’s resolution margin. This should retain a zero time penalty and may reach the maximum CRF of 1.0.

Increase the final organic fraction one grid step to test a slightly faster separation while retaining the maximum CRF. Recent trends suggest the closest pair may gain a little resolution while the neighboring pair remains above 1.5.

With the maximum CRF already achieved, test an alternative that may provide a larger resolution margin. Higher temperature should further separate the previously limiting pair, while a shallower gradient may protect the neighboring pair without introducing a time penalty.

Return to 55 °C and test a higher starting organic fraction with a shallower gradient to seek a wider resolution margin at the maximum CRF. The higher starting strength should offset some of the added gradient time while probing selectivity in the crowded middle region.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction further improves the limiting pair, using a shallower gradient to protect neighboring separations. This explores a potentially larger resolution margin while aiming to keep the last peak below the time-penalty threshold.

Slightly steepen the gradient relative to injection 11 to shorten the separation while testing whether its improved resolution margin is retained. This nearby method may also achieve CRF 1.000 with all adjacent pairs above 1.5.

Slightly flatten the gradient relative to injection 11 to improve the newly limiting neighboring pair while checking that the last peak remains below the time-penalty threshold. The maximum CRF is already established; this test seeks another maximum-scoring method with a useful resolution margin.

Test a shallower gradient at the starting composition of injection 10 to map the neighborhood that preserves maximum CRF. This should improve the earlier close pair while checking whether the later close pair remains fully resolved without a time penalty.

Test the intermediate endpoint between injections 10 and 14, both of which achieved maximum CRF. This should retain full resolution and zero time penalty while providing another nearby operating point in the maximum-scoring region.

This gradient slope lies between those of injections 11 and 13, which both achieved maximum CRF with minimum resolution of at least 1.67. Test this nearby method to confirm another fully resolved operating point with no time penalty.

Test a lower final organic fraction with a gradient slope between those of maximum-scoring injections 10 and 15. This should preserve full resolution and zero time penalty while checking whether a lower endpoint is sufficient for all 10 compounds.

Slightly steepen the gradient from injection 17 to shorten retention and potentially improve the later close pair while preserving the earlier pair’s resolution margin. This tests a nearby candidate for maintaining CRF 1.000 with a faster separation.

Test a modestly steeper gradient than injection 18, targeting a shorter separation while retaining both close pairs above R = 1.5. The lower endpoint should still be sufficient because all peaks are expected to elute before the gradient ends.

Test a lower endpoint with a gradient slope between those of maximum-scoring injections 11 and 12. This should preserve full resolution and zero time penalty while extending the tested range of maximum-scoring methods.

Use the same starting composition, temperature, and gradient slope as maximum-scoring injection 8, but finish the gradient earlier at a lower endpoint. Since its last peak eluted before this proposed gradient ends, the separation should remain essentially unchanged.

Preserve the gradient slope of injections 8 and 21 while lowering the endpoint and shortening the programmed gradient again. The gradient should still extend beyond the last peak, so the maximum-scoring separation is expected to be retained.

Keep the successful gradient slope but begin the final hold after the first nine peaks and before the last peak. This tests whether a lower endpoint can retain maximum CRF without delaying the last compound enough to incur a time penalty.

Preserve the starting composition, temperature, and gradient slope of injection 18 while lowering the endpoint to 0.60. Since the outlet gradient ends at 8.65 minutes, after the previously observed last peak at 8.00 minutes, this should retain its maximum CRF and resolution margin.

Test a shorter programmed gradient with a slope close to injection 11, which achieved maximum CRF and a minimum resolution of 1.70. The last peak is expected before the outlet gradient ends at 10.65 minutes, preserving full resolution and zero time penalty.
